newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance credit facility extended.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance credit facility extended.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co. said Wednesday that Bank of America agreed to extend its $50 million credit facility, under existing terms, through Jan. 6, 1998.
Mercury, which makes consumer and auto loans, defaulted on short-term lending agreements in February after discovering accounting discrepancies that forced it to restate four years' earnings.
It faces a federal investigation, several shareholder lawsuits, and a major loss in market capitalisation after its stock price plunged.
The credit facility included waivers, which expired Tuesday, that enable the company to pledge assets to back the BankAmerica Corp. unit's loan.
The Chicago-based company said it is continuing negotiations to obtain the extension of creditor waivers.
No funds are currently outstanding to Bank of America under the credit facility, and none have been outstanding since the line was repaid in May, Mercury said.
Mercury said cash flow position is positive, and it does not see a need to borrow any funds now or in the near future.
"In fact, we never utilized more than $10 million of the line for operational purposes," company President William Brandt Jr. said in a statement.
"Indeed, we have been able to pay expenses from cash flow, including interest on all of our indebtedness."
Mercury said it remains committed to complete the 1996 audit of financial statements as early as possible, and in line with estimates released in April.
First-quarter results should be released soon after that, it said.
Mercury's stock rose 25 cents to $2.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in consolidated early afternoon trading.
